title: Conflict Protocol
concept: The full path through a conflict: check if you're calm enough to talk, warm up, make sure it's safe, say what happened, ask for one thing, and follow through.
whenToUse: Use during an active conflict, or a fight you keep having, as long as you can still be warm with each other (or once a Pause has brought you back to calm).
steps: Check if you're calm — overwhelmed? Take a Pause + Return first.
Warm up — say one warm, true thing.
Make it safe — remind each other you're not breaking up.
Say what happened — “When X happened, I felt Y; here's the impact.”
Ask for one thing — be specific.
Listen in the right order — impact first, helping second, their side of it last.
Get proof if you need it — a change, evidence it happened, and a set time to check.
Line up next steps — who does what, and when you'll check back.

phrases.text: I’m on your team, even though I’m frustrated.
Can we soften the room first?
I think we’re stuck in a Reach–Recoil loop — 20-minute pause?

working: Warmth got through → said what happened → asked for one thing → booked a time to check in. The fight stops repeating instead of turning into a trial.
notWorking: Skip the warm-up and go straight to cross-examining each other. One person pushes, the other shuts down, and it locks up. Fix: bank a few warm-up phrases and check the other person actually heard them before moving on.
activity: Practice once on something low-stakes, with a timer. Whoever's listening makes sure the order is followed.
